scope: Native package map publication and per-command graph selection. No application input latency or all-platform threading claim.
problem: Concurrent package commands truncate and rewrite one module-map.tsv. Readers can observe an empty or partial file, and an earlier command can receive a later command's different graph.
change: Publish files from exclusively owned private temporary files, synchronize and close them, then atomically rename into place. Failed publication removes only its own temporary.
Give every compiler invocation a SHA-256 content-specific map path. Identical graph content uses the same snapshot path. Different graphs cannot replace the path passed to another child.
Keep module-map.tsv as the latest complete map for local inspection. Compiler children use their content-specific snapshot.

before_regression.fixture_correction: The initially incomplete fixture was corrected to provide its own empty standard-module root before comparing original and changed implementations.

package_integration.scope: Existing package lock, aliases, two dependency revisions, templates, bootstrap launcher and compiler backend checks; only generated local Git fixtures are cloned. Canonical tool sources are used through overrides.

actual_harmony_parallel_commands.scope: Eight source checks and eight C generations using the actual Harmony dependency graph, with no GUI or installed runtime changes.

matched_launcher.method: Original canonical generated launcher objects shared; add only PkgWriteAtomic and replace only PkgWriteMap. All unrelated current scanner/compiler edits are excluded.

deployment.intended: Install only the verified matched native package launcher, preserving all existing compiler siblings and ongoing processes.

limitations: This fixes concurrency correctness in package commands; it establishes no new Harmony responsiveness gain.
Graph snapshots are generated build-cache artifacts. Distinct graph contents create distinct files; normal build cleanup removes the cache.
Native C/C++ and Linux fixtures were executed. No new physical Android, Windows, macOS or Plan 9 execution in this change.
Other mutable package artifacts, such as the lock and option files, have separate lifecycles and still require a full concurrent-writer audit.
next_action: Continue the terminal request path using output notifications and bounded persistent transport; do not infer runtime 10x progress from a package build concurrency repair.
